title: Cavity-QED enhancement of quantum entanglement and battery performance in double quantum dots
authors: Hamid Arian Zad, Usama Shoukat, Michal Jaščur, Hazrat Ali, Saeed Haddadi
abstract: We theoretically investigate quantum correlations and energy storage in a single-electron silicon double quantum dot (eDQD) coupled to a single-mode microwave cavity. The charge and spin degrees of freedom are hybridized by Rashba spin-orbit coupling (SOC), while the cavity interacts with the eDQD through spin-photon and charge-photon couplings. Using the reduced thermal density matrix, we characterize spin-charge entanglement by concurrence and quantum coherence by the $l_1$ norm. At low temperature, the cavity strongly modifies the spin-charge correlations, producing distinct regimes of enhanced and suppressed entanglement. We identify a nonlinear crossover between an eDQD-dominated regime and a photon-dressed regime. This crossover is revealed independently by two signatures: a rapid change in the concurrence and the onset of finite photon occupation in the cavity. Its boundary exhibits a dominant $G_{\rm c}\propto\sqrtΩ$ dependence and is robust against cavity Hilbert-space truncation. Beyond the Rashba coupling studied in [Ferreira et al., Phys. Rev. A 107, 052408 (2023)], we show that the cavity provides an additional tunable means of controlling quantum correlations and energy storage. We further characterize the eDQD as a quantum battery under coherent charging and evaluate its stored energy and ergotropy. The ergotropy varies markedly across a cavity-dressing crossover resembling that identified from entanglement, connecting cavity-induced modification of the dressed states to extractable work. Optimization over the charge-photon coupling reveals parameter-dependent optimal charging regimes and enhanced maximum ergotropy with increasing Rashba coupling. Our results establish cavity coupling and SOC as complementary controls of quantum correlations and extractable energy in semiconductor eDQD-cavity systems.
summary: This theoretical study explores the interplay between quantum entanglement and energy storage in a silicon double quantum dot coupled to a microwave cavity. By analyzing the system's reduced density matrix, the authors show that cavity coupling and spin-orbit coupling provide complementary control over quantum correlations. A key finding is that the crossover regime governing entanglement is mirrored in the system's extractable work (ergotropy), establishing a unified control mechanism for quantum resources.
main_problem: The study investigates how coupling a single-electron double quantum dot (eDQD) to a microwave cavity affects both quantum entanglement and the system's capacity for energy storage.
main_result: The cavity coupling and Rashba SOC act as complementary control knobs, creating a distinct crossover regime that simultaneously modifies quantum correlations (concurrence) and the extractable work (ergotropy).
method: The authors use theoretical methods involving the reduced thermal density matrix, calculating entanglement via concurrence and coherence via the l1 norm, alongside energy metrics like ergotropy.
model_or_system: The system is an eDQD coupled to a single-mode microwave cavity, incorporating Rashba spin-orbit coupling, spin-photon, and charge-photon interactions. The Hamiltonian describes the coupled charge, spin, and cavity modes.
key_observables: Concurrence (spin-charge entanglement), l1-norm of coherence, ergotropy (extractable work), and stored energy.
important_parameters: Rashba coupling strength ($\alpha$), cavity coupling strengths ($G, g_c$), cavity frequency ($\Omega$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on tracing out the cavity degrees of freedom to find the reduced eDQD state, and it examines the system in its thermal equilibrium state.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of ergotropy, stored energy, and concurrence on coupling parameters, highlighting a sharp, nonlinear crossover boundary in the parameter space.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model (eDQD-cavity-SOC), analyzes quantum correlations (entanglement/coherence) using the reduced density matrix, and then extends the analysis to energy storage by calculating ergotropy and showing its correlation with the entanglement crossover.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics as it models quantum control in solid-state cavity QED systems, linking fundamental quantum information measures (entanglement) directly to practical quantum technologies (quantum batteries).

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic representation of an eDQD embedded in a microwave cavity QED. The electron can tunnel between the left and right dots with amplitude J, experiencing Rashba SOC α that mixes spin and charge degrees of freedom. B is the Zeeman splitting as a result of a homogeneous magnetic field along the z-axis. The cavity mode of frequency Ωcouples to the electron spin via the Jaynes–Cummings interaction of strength G, enabling coherent spin-photon exchange.

FIG. 2. Concurrence C of the eDQD system in the G/J-Ω/J plane at kBT/J = 0.01 for (a) α/J = 1, (b) α/J = 2, and (c) α/J = 10. The symbolic blue lines indicate the crossover boundary extracted from the maximum variation of the concurrence, maxG |∂C/∂G| at fixed Ωsatisfying Eq. (14). This boundary closely coincides with the independently determined ground-state crossover associated with the onset of appreciable cavity-photon occupation. In three panels we have assumed, B/J = 2, N = 5 and gc/J = 0.

FIG. 3. The concurrence of the eDQD system in the G/J − T/J plane at Ω/J = 5. (a) α/J = 1, (b) α/J = 2. The upper insets represent the concurrence, while the lower insets show the l1-norm coherence Cl1, providing a complementary mea- sure of the quantum coherence underlying the reduced eDQD state. The dotted curves in the insets show the corresponding results for the eDQD without the cavity with G/J = Ω/J = 0, while the solid curves represent the cavity-coupled eDQD sys- tem with G/J = 3 and Ω/J = 5. In all panels, we have as- sumed: B/J = 2, gc/J = 0, N = 5.
FIG. 4. The concurrence of the eDQD system in the gc/J − Ω/J plane at kBT/J = 0.01 and G/J = 3. (a) α/J = 1, (b) α/J = 2. In both panels we have assumed: B/J = 2 and N = 5.

FIG. 5. Schematic representation of the cavity-mediated eDQD QB. The eDQD, comprising coupled charge and spin degrees of freedom, constitutes the QB, while a single-mode microwave cavity mediates the interaction between the bat- tery and the charging process. The charge and spin sectors are coupled through the Rashba SOC with strength α, while J denotes the inter-dot tunneling amplitude and B the de- tuning energy. The cavity couples to the DQD spin degree of freedom through the Jaynes–Cummings interaction with strength G, and to the charge degree of freedom through gc.
